subject: Reactivity does not work when I change input by javascript

messages.author: 2a04630187a7758b
messages.subject: Reactivity does not work when I change input by javascript
parts:
Hi guys,

I noticed that when I have some input and I change its value by javascript (e.g. when the users clicks on abutton an input checkbox gets checked by the script), shiny does not recalculate although the html part works fine (the checkbox gets, in fact, checked on the webpage). If I display the box, "manually" checking the box works fine.

Does anyone have the same experience? Is there a way around it or is it a limitation of Shiny?

Peter

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Reactivity does not work when I change input by javascript
parts:
Two issues here.

1) The <select> and <input type="checkbox"> both need id attributes, not name. (Or it's OK to have name, but you must also have id.)

2) If that alone doesn't fix it, try adding this after you set the selected index:
$("#fixed_float").change();

Please let me know if that works for you; if so, and you need further explanation about why that fixes it, I would be happy to explain.

Taking a step back, though, if you're presenting two mutually-exclusive sets of inputs or outputs, you might be better served with using tabsetPanel (note that if you give tabsetPanel an inputId, then your R code can know which tab is active); and if you prefer not to use tabsetPanel, then at least checkboxGroupInput for the Fixed/Float choice and use conditionalPanel to hide/show the relevant controls. As far as I can see, everything you want to do here can be accomplished entirely using Shiny features, no JavaScript required.

Joe,

I was trying to use getElementById previously and it did not work so 1) did not help and I must have programmed 2) incorrectly (just added it as next line) because it did not do anything.

However, your suggestion of .change(), made to realize that for shiny to re-execute I need not just change the value of the input but simulate as if the user clicked with a mouse. It lead to more elegant solution, instead of:

     var checkbox = document.getElementById('ff');
     checkbox.checked = true;

I now have just this

     document.getElementById('ff').click();

Problem solved. Thanks:-)

Peter
